html:
The Darvaza gas crater, known as the Door to Hell, is a burning pit in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan, about 70 metres across, which has been on fire for decades.

The usual story is that Soviet geologists drilling for gas around 1971 broke into a cavern, the rig fell in, and the crater was set alight to burn off the gas. Turkmen geologists have said it collapsed in the 1960s and was lit in the 1980s. No record settles it.

It became the country's best known sight for the few foreign tourists allowed in. In 2022 the president ordered the fire put out to save gas, which Turkmenistan holds in some of the largest reserves on earth, as at Galkynysh. It still burns at a lower level.
sum: The Darvaza gas crater, known as the Door to Hell, is a burning pit in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan, about 70 metres across, which has been on fire for decades.
